2609.35677.title: Verifier Errors in RLVR: Reward Hacking, Limits of Feedback, and Selective Control
2609.35677.paper_summary: In reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), imperfect verifiers can reward incorrect responses, creating opportunities for reward hacking. Using gradient flow with a fixed verifier, we characterize the conditions under which reward rises while correctness falls. We then show that the observations available during RLVR are, in general, insufficient to detect or identify accepted errors, or to guarantee their reduction without sacrificing correct responses. To address this limit, we construct a correction using additional feedback about correctness from audits. This correction achieves \emph{selective control}: at the current policy, it lowers the probability of accepted errors and raises that of correct responses, provided it outweighs the pressure toward errors from verifier reward. Experiments with log linear and neural contextual bandits and with a language model support the analysis and show that selective control under partial auditing reduces accepted errors while increasing correctness.
2609.35677.paper_summary_zh: 在具有可驗證獎勵的強化學習（RLVR）中，不完美的驗證者可能會對不正確的回應給予獎勵，從而創造了獎勵駭客的機會。使用固定驗證者的梯度流，我們描述了獎勵上升而正確性下降的條件。然後我們顯示，在一般情況下，RLVR 中可用的觀察不足以檢測或識別被接受的錯誤，或在不犧牲正確回應的情況下保證其減少。為了解決這一限制，我們構建了一個使用來自審核的正確性附加反饋的修正。這個修正實現了 \emph{選擇性控制}：在當前策略下，它降低了被接受錯誤的概率，並提高了正確回應的概率，前提是它超過了來自驗證者獎勵的錯誤壓力。對於對數線性和神經上下文賭徒以及語言模型的實驗支持了這一分析，並顯示在部分審核下的選擇性控制減少了被接受的錯誤，同時提高了正確性。
